---
title: "Feature selection for cell-type Gaussians"
---

This chapter selects a gene panel $\mathcal{G}$ on which DeCovarT can
discriminate gastruloid cell types through **both** mean shifts
$\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}$ and precision rewiring
$\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}\equiv\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}^{-1}$. Notation follows
the article: gene $g=1,\ldots,G$; cell type $j=1,\ldots,J$; bulk
$\boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot i}$ is a Gaussian convolution of purified profiles
[@wangBulkTissueCell2019]. Feature selection is a pre-modelling filter
[@guyonIntroductionVariableFeature2003], not a marker-enrichment score.

The first pipeline treated `sctransform` highly variable genes (HVGs),
optional `DESeq2` on technical pseudo-bulks, and an NSGA-II Pareto
refinement as a single stack. That mix is too optimistic on
**Suppinger**, where there is only **one** scRNA-seq resource (GEO
[GSE229513](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE229513);
[@suppingerMultimodalCharacterizationMurine2023]), and it puts variance
stabilisation on the same design axis as the graphical model (see
@sec-grn-observation and @nte-jensen-transform). Here we split the
problem into a **naive screen** (cheap, marginally motivated) and an
**all-versus-all refinement** (geometry of $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}}$
and rewiring of $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$). `INDEED` and D-trace enter only
as a **perspective** (@sec-fs-perspective).

# Notation {#sec-fs-notation}

Let $\boldsymbol{\mu}=(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j})_{j=1}^{J}\in\mathbb{R}^{G\times J}$
be the mean signature and $\{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}\}_{j=1}^{J}$ the
cell-type covariances. Conditionally on proportions
$\boldsymbol{p}\in\Delta^{J-1}$,

$$
\boldsymbol{y}\mid(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})
\sim
\mathcal{N}_{G}\!\left(
\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p},\,
\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_{j}^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}
\right),
\quad
\boldsymbol{\zeta}=(\boldsymbol{\mu},\{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}\}),
$$ {#eq-fs-mixture}

which is the DeCovarT convolution (article Methods; the same
$p_{j}^{2}$ scaling appears in the first pipeline's aggregation algebra,
corrected in @sec-align-invariance). For a subset
$\mathcal{G}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,G\}$ write $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}}$
for the corresponding rows. The 2-norm condition number is

$$
\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{X})
=
\frac{\sigma_{\max}(\boldsymbol{X})}{\sigma_{\min}(\boldsymbol{X})}.
$$ {#eq-fs-kappa}

Large $\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}})$ is multicollinearity of
the **mean** design [@gongDeconRNASeqStatisticalFramework2013;
@newmanRobustEnumerationCell2015]. It does **not** see precision
rewiring. For a gastruloid continuum, neighbouring states are close in
mean by construction; aggressive $\kappa$-minimisation then keeps a few
lineage representatives and drops genes whose signal lives in
$\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ [@wangBulkTissueCell2019].

::: {#nte-linear-scale .callout-important}
## :warning: Keep the mixture on a linear scale

@eq-fs-mixture is linear in $\boldsymbol{p}$ only if $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and
$\boldsymbol{y}$ live on the **same additive scale** (counts, CPM, or TPM).
Logarithms, `SCTransform` Pearson residuals, and nonparanormal scores
break that map [@sturmComprehensiveEvaluationTranscriptomebased2019;
@jinBenchmarkRNAseqDeconvolution2021;
@hoffmannRobustComputationalReconstitution2006]. Use residualisation
only to **rank** HVGs (@sec-fs-hvg); export DeCovarT moments on the
linear scale. The probabilistic reason is Jensen's inequality: see
@nte-jensen-transform.
:::

# Naive screen {#sec-fs-naive}

The naive stage builds a working universe $\mathcal{G}_{0}$ of a few
thousand genes. It is **one-versus-rest in spirit**: each gene is scored
marginally. That is cheap and biologically readable, and it is the right
place to stop if the all-versus-all optimiser has nothing to search
over. It is the **wrong** place to stop for DeCovarT, because
concatenating per-type shortlists typically yields a multicollinear
$\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}}$ [@newmanRobustEnumerationCell2015].

## Highly variable genes {#sec-fs-hvg}

Single-cell UMI tables mix depth noise with biological heterogeneity.
Regularised negative-binomial regression in `sctransform` [@R-sctransform]
/ `Seurat::SCTransform` separates the two via Pearson residuals
[@hafemeisterNormalizationVarianceStabilization2019]

$$
r_{cg}
=
\frac{y_{cg}-\hat{\mu}_{cg}}
{\sqrt{\hat{\mu}_{cg}+\hat{\mu}_{cg}^{2}/\hat{\theta}_{g}}},
$$ {#eq-fs-pearson}

with library size as an offset and empirical-Bayes shrinkage of
dispersions $\hat{\theta}_{g}$. Residual variance is a ranking score
for HVGs, **not** a Gaussian observation model for graphical lasso.

Practical rules for Suppinger:

1.  Do **not** regress out cell type when ranking HVGs: that removes
    the inter-type signal the panel is meant to keep.
2.  A design $\sim\texttt{CellType}$ without intercept contrasts each
    labelled type against the global mean across types, which is closer
    to an all-versus-all HVG ranking than a global intercept.
3.  Keep on the order of $2{,}000$ residual-variable genes as
    $\mathcal{G}_{0}$ before any GGM; estimating
    $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ on the full transcriptome is unstable when
    $G\gg n_{j}$ even with glasso
    [@friedmanSparseInverseCovariance2008].
4.  `SCTransform` is **tied to HVG ranking**, not a factorial
    “normalisation arm” of the GRN design (@sec-grn-observation).

::: {#nte-hvg-not-gaussian .callout-note}
## :information_source: HVGs are not a GGM input

Pearson residuals are closer to homoscedastic than raw UMI counts, which
is why they are popular before PCA. They are still a **nonlinear
residualisation**. Feeding them indiscriminately into `SILGGM` silently
changes the estimand of $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ away from the latent
Gaussian that DeCovarT wants at the **population** level. If a Gaussian
GGM is used, prefer a copula / nonparanormal map on the same gene set
(@sec-silggm), or better a Poisson-lognormal latent Gaussian
(@sec-pln).
:::

## Marker genes {#sec-fs-markers}

Classical signatures score gene $g$ for type $j$ against the remaining
types, then concatenate lists [@newmanRobustEnumerationCell2015]. Two
specificity scores on the simplex of relative means

$$
\pi_{gj}
=
\frac{\mu_{gj}}{\sum_{\ell=1}^{J}\mu_{g\ell}},
\qquad
\sum_{j}\pi_{gj}=1,
$$ {#eq-fs-shares}

are useful **compaction** tools, not all-versus-all selectors.

**Shannon entropy** $H(g)=-\sum_{j}\pi_{gj}\log\pi_{gj}$ is small when
mass concentrates on few types. **Gini** of the same shares is large
when one type dominates. High Gini / low entropy flags one-versus-rest
markers. They do not guarantee that the corresponding rows of
$\boldsymbol{\mu}$ are linearly independent: two markers that separate
*different* types can still be collinear as rows if those types co-express
a shared programme. Concatenating the top-$k$ genes per type therefore
often inflates $|\mathcal{G}|$ without improving $\kappa_{2}$ (see
@nte-ovr-concat).

Known gastruloid lineage markers (from the Suppinger atlas and
companion literature) belong in $\mathcal{G}_{0}$ as **seeds**, not as
the whole panel. They are the natural starting points for Markov-boundary
expansion once a GGM exists (@sec-fs-perspective).

## Differential expression — only with biological replication {#sec-fs-deg}

`DESeq2`, `edgeR` and `limma`–voom remain the workhorses of one-versus-rest
ranking [@loveModeratedEstimationFold2014]. CIBERSORT-style pipelines
keep genes with a loose adjusted $p$ ordered by fold-change, then prune
by $\kappa$ [@newmanRobustEnumerationCell2015]. That logic **does not
transfer** to Suppinger as a DE experiment.

::: {#nte-pseudoreplication .callout-warning}
## :warning: Technical pseudo-bulks are not biological replicates

Cells from a common experimental unit are not independent biological
replicates. Splitting or bootstrapping cells characterises
**technical / sampling** variability; it does not manufacture
between-organoid uncertainty. Treating cells, or random partitions of
cells, as `DESeq2` replicates inflates apparent degrees of freedom and
produces false discoveries [@squairConfrontingFalseDiscoveries2021;
@crowellMuscatDetectsSubpopulationspecific2020]. The improved pipeline
is explicit: Suppinger is **one** technical scRNA-seq resource.

Use `DESeq2` in this book only if **independent biological replicates**
exist (distinct organoids / donors / experiments with the same labelled
types). For GSE229513, skip calibrated DE $p$-values. Rank genes by
residual variance, Gini / entropy, or a nested-model $F$ statistic
treated as a **score**, not as a $p$-value.
:::

If a later gastruloid cohort with genuine replication becomes
available (GSE250136 is a *different* stem-embryo resource, useful as
external validation, not as extra Suppinger replicates), then
donor-level pseudo-bulks are the correct DE unit
[@crowellMuscatDetectsSubpopulationspecific2020;
@squairConfrontingFalseDiscoveries2021]. Until then, the naive screen
is HVG + markers, not HVG + `DESeq2`.

::: {#nte-ovr-concat .callout-warning}
## :warning: Limitation of one-versus-rest concatenation

The union of per-type markers is usually a multicollinear
$\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}}$ that is still too large for stable
NNLS / GLS / DeCovarT Fisher information
[@newmanRobustEnumerationCell2015]. A global all-versus-all stage is
required (@sec-fs-advanced).
:::

# All-versus-all refinement {#sec-fs-advanced}

The advanced stage treats $\mathcal{G}$ as a **subset selection**
problem on the full $J$-column signature. The loss is defined on all
types jointly. That is the right geometry for DeCovarT: the likelihood
depends on $\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}$ **and** on
$\sum_{j}p_{j}^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}$, so genes that only separate one
type from “the rest” can still leave two gastruloid neighbours
unidentifiable.

## Why mean-only $\kappa$ is not enough {#sec-fs-kappa}

$\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}})$ diagnoses mean collinearity.
In a gastruloid continuum it is intrinsically large. Two closely related
types can share nearly collinear means and still differ in
$\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$. Mean-only pruning then under-represents
adjacent or low-abundance states — exactly the types whose **rewiring**
DeCovarT is meant to exploit. Use $\kappa$ as a **diagnostic**, not as
the sole selector.

A variance-weighted variant standardises rows by gene-wise
uncertainties $\tau_{g}^{2}$ and evaluates conditioning in the
$(J-1)$-dimensional contrast space induced by $\sum_{j}p_{j}=1$
(package vignette `supp-S6-feature-selection.qmd`). Unweighted $\kappa$
can favour quiet but biased genes
[@gongDeconRNASeqStatisticalFramework2013].

## Genetic algorithms {#sec-fs-ga}

`AutoGeneS` searches subsets with a multi-objective genetic algorithm
that minimises inter-population correlation while maximising centroid
distance [@alieeAutoGeneSAutomaticGene2021]. The loss is already
all-versus-all. Related multi-objective genetic searches appear in
network module discovery; they are not DeCovarT-specific.

For this repository the planned optimiser is NSGA-II via `mco::nsga2()`
[@R-mco], as in the package vignette. Encode genes as a mask in
$[0,1]^{|\mathcal{G}_{0}|}$ (thresholded to a target size) or as a
lower-dimensional embedding of gene blocks. Minimise at least

1.  $\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}})$ (mean geometry);
2.  average pairwise overlap $\overline{\omega}$ of the $J$ Gaussians
    $\mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j})$
    [@melnykovMixSimPackageSimulating2012; @R-MixSim].

`MixSim` defines pairwise overlap as the **sum of the two
misclassification probabilities** under a Bayes / MAP rule, not as
$1$ minus a distance. That is a sharper estimand than “one minus
Hellinger”. Optional analytic surrogates — Jeffreys (symmetric KL),
Chernoff / Bhattacharyya, and the Bures–Wasserstein metric on
$(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j})$ — belong on the same
Pareto front (package vignette). They use **both** means and
covariances, which `AutoGeneS` correlation / centroid objectives do not.

::: {#nte-pareto-proposal .callout-note}
## :information_source: A DeCovarT-specific third objective (proposal)

The improved pipeline proposed adding Fisher identifiability of
$\boldsymbol{p}$ under @eq-fs-mixture: maximise the smallest eigenvalue of
the mixture information $I_{\mathcal{G}}(\boldsymbol{p})$, or minimise its
condition number. That objective is **not** in the literature corpus; it
is a composition. It is the right scientific target — DeCovarT's score
depends on $\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}$ and
$\sum_{j}p_{j}^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}$ jointly — but it is
proportion-dependent and more expensive than MixSim overlap. Keep it as
a **sensitivity objective** on a shortlist of non-dominated panels, not
as the only fitness. Do not collapse the front to a single “knee”
without nested, leakage-free validation.
:::

Keep several non-dominated panels. Report the whole front. Nested
cross-validation, when biological replicates exist, must build HVGs,
DEGs and the Pareto panel **inside** each outer fold; otherwise the
panel leaks [@squairConfrontingFalseDiscoveries2021]. With one
Suppinger resource, the honest statement is: the panel is fitted on this
atlas and must be challenged on an external gastruloid cohort.

## Differential networks as candidate generators {#sec-fs-diffnet}

DeCovarT benefits specifically from **rewiring** between populations.
A gene that changes neighbourhood in $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ is a better
candidate than a gene that is merely highly variable. Two strategies
exist.

**Fit every $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$, then compare supports.** Independent
glasso / `SILGGM` fits (@sec-silggm) yield per-type edges; the symmetric
difference of supports, or the difference of partial correlations, ranks
genes by differential connectivity. This is simple and matches the
objects DeCovarT eventually needs, but each glasso is shrunk and the
difference of two biased estimators is not a debiased estimator of
$\Delta_{j\ell}=\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}-\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{\ell}$.

**Estimate $\Delta_{j\ell}$ directly.** D-trace methods target the
difference of precisions without necessarily reconstructing both graphs
first (see @sec-fs-perspective). They cannot replace
$\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ in the generative model — DeCovarT still needs
each covariance individually — but they are attractive **feature
objectives** when individual networks are fairly dense and the
*difference* is sparse.

Either way, treat differential-network hits as **candidates** for the
all-versus-all stage, not as the final panel. Concatenating one-versus-rest
network genes repeats @nte-ovr-concat.

# Perspectives: `INDEED` and D-trace {#sec-fs-perspective}

These methods are **not** in the core Suppinger pipeline. They are the
statistically natural next step when (i) two (or $J$) groups are to be
compared as networks, and (ii) genes that both shift in mean **and**
rewire are the desired biomarkers. Full detail lives in DeCovarT
`vignettes/supp-S6-feature-selection.qmd`; we only import the estimands.

## `INDEED`: an ad-hoc fusion of DE and differential partial correlation

`INDEED` fits a sparse precision per group, converts to partial
correlations

$$
\mathrm{pc}_{gg'}^{(j)}
=
-\frac{\theta_{gg'}^{(j)}}
{\sqrt{\theta_{gg}^{(j)}\,\theta_{g'g'}^{(j)}}},
\qquad
\Delta\mathrm{pc}_{gg'}
=
\mathrm{pc}_{gg'}^{(j)}-\mathrm{pc}_{gg'}^{(\ell)},
$$ {#eq-indeed-dpc}

filters $\Delta\mathrm{pc}$ with a permutation (or bootstrap) null, and
forms an activity score that multiplies mean evidence by differential
connectivity [@zuoINDEEDIntegratedDifferential2016]

$$
\mathrm{AS}_{g}
=
\bigl(-\log p_{g}^{\mathrm{DE}}\bigr)
\sum_{g'\neq g}
\bigl\lvert\Delta\mathrm{pc}_{gg'}\bigr\rvert
\,
\mathbf{1}\{\Delta\mathrm{pc}_{gg'}\ \text{significant}\}.
$$ {#eq-indeed-as}

Relative to pure DGE, this favours genes whose **undirected**
neighbourhood (Markov boundary in the GGM) differs between groups.
Related ideas appear in weighted glasso pipelines with PPI priors.

**Criticism for Suppinger.** The DE $p$-value in @eq-indeed-as assumes
biological replication (@nte-pseudoreplication). The permutation null on
$\Delta\mathrm{pc}$ among cells of one gastruloid is again a technical
null. `INDEED` is also **ad hoc**: it tests edges after two separate
glasso fits rather than estimating $\Delta$ under a joint loss. Use it,
if at all, as a ranking heuristic on $\mathcal{G}_{0}$, with
$p_{g}^{\mathrm{DE}}$ replaced by a fold-change or $F$ score.

## D-trace: a loss that targets $\Delta=\Theta_{j}-\Theta_{\ell}$

Zhang and Zou [@zhangSparsePrecisionMatrix2014] introduced the
lasso-penalised D-trace loss for a **single** sparse precision, with an
alternating-direction algorithm and sparse-recovery guarantees under an
irrepresentability condition that can hold when the analogous condition
for lasso-penalised Gaussian likelihood fails. In the same paper they
note that the graphical lasso estimator of a sparse precision is usually
still consistent for the **support** of the true direct interactions
even when the data are not multivariate Gaussian. That is useful
background for our glasso / `SILGGM` branch: off-Gaussian UMI tables
need not destroy edge recovery, even though they do destroy the
interpretation of $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Theta}}_{j}$ as a Gaussian
generative precision.

The differential-network extension
[@yuanDifferentialNetworkAnalysis2017] estimates a sparse difference
$\Delta_{j\ell}=\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}-\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{\ell}$. Empirically,
D-trace is competitive for differential-network recovery when the
**difference** is sparser than either graph, although hubs and dense
networks remain difficult [@plaksienkoMethodsDifferentialNetwork2025].

For DeCovarT this is the cleaner **perspective** than `INDEED`:

-   the estimand $\Delta_{j\ell}$ is exactly “which partial
    correlations rewire”;
-   it does not require a calibrated DE $p$-value;
-   it still does **not** produce a pair of SPD
    $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j},\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{\ell}$ suitable as generative
    covariances.

A workable composition — labelled as a **proposal**, not as a result —
is: use D-trace (or debiased fused graphical lasso) to **nominate**
rewiring genes; retain those genes in $\mathcal{G}$; then estimate each
$\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ on $\mathcal{G}$ with a method from
@sec-grn-top4 that returns an SPD precision.

## Markov boundaries as panel expansion

Once a GGM exists, a small set of seeds (markers, HVG hubs, `INDEED` /
D-trace hits) can be grown by undirected neighbours
$\{g':\theta_{gg'}\neq 0\}$. In a Gaussian Markov random field those
neighbours are the Markov boundary: they carry residual information
about $g$ given the rest of the genes. This is **undirected**
conditioning, not DAG $d$-separation. Directed path-blocking rules are
the wrong language for glasso supports.

# What we would actually run on Suppinger {#sec-fs-recommend}

1.  **Naive screen.** `SCTransform` (or residual variance from a
    depth-aware NB) to rank HVGs; add curated gastruloid markers;
    **no** `DESeq2` $p$-values on technical pseudo-bulks.
2.  **Cap $|\mathcal{G}_{0}|$.** A few thousand genes before any GGM.
3.  **All-versus-all.** NSGA-II on $\kappa_{2}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}})$
    and MixSim $\overline{\omega}$, optionally with Jeffreys / Chernoff
    as diagnostics. Keep the Pareto set.
4.  **Optional DiffNet candidates.** Symmetric difference of per-type
    `SILGGM` supports, or D-trace on a pair of abundant types, as extra
    genes in $\mathcal{G}_{0}$ — not as the panel.
5.  **Export linear-scale** $\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\mathcal{G}}$ and
    $\boldsymbol{\Theta}_{j}$ into DeCovarT.

The first pipeline's “HVG then DESeq2 then NSGA-II on $\kappa$ and
overlap” is directionally right but overstates what one gastruloid
scRNA-seq experiment can support, and it treats variance stabilisation
as if it were a harmless preprocessing for the mixture. The improved
pipeline's Fisher-information objective is scientifically tighter and
should be treated as a **proposal** until it is computed.

Scripts (when implemented): `scripts/04_01_*.R` (screen) and
`scripts/04_02_*.R` (Pareto). No code is given here.
